purpose: Contract governance, SDK distribution and cross-repository compatibility. Not a runtime gateway.

services.auth: Appwrite session JWT; Backend validates and derives identity
services.notes: Backend is the only public product API runtime and canonical authority for local and remote social relationships, public posts and privacy. It transactionally enqueues opted-in public posts for Federation and rechecks public eligibility on object dereference.

services.auth: Obtains Appwrite JWT and sends it only to Backend public API
services.notes: Must never call private services, PostgreSQL, storage credentials, Federation or Algorithm directly.

services.auth: PLATFORM_INTERNAL_TOKEN for protected writes; public config read is restricted to enabled public keys
services.notes: The pinned Backend mainline contains a typed Data Centre media client and matching client tests for all five private media lifecycle routes (upload-url, verify, status, download-url and delete). API cross-repository CI statically verifies those routes against the Data Centre handler, OpenAPI snapshot, Backend Compose network and dedicated service-token wiring. This does not yet prove live B2/R2 provider write/read/hash/replication/delete/restore behavior. The separate Data Centre platform event/audit/config API still has no verified typed Backend client; do not conflate it with the media lifecycle service. Video and notification services require separately audited contracts.

services.auth: Public objects by policy; private media requires expiring key-bound playback authorization; purge uses PURGE_TOKEN
services.notes: The pinned Go CDN requires a trusted origin service credential for readiness and private requests, forwards the Backend viewer assertion and separate origin credential, requires the Backend origin to classify public objects explicitly, bypasses shared cache for private responses (private, no-store), and has tests for denial, origin failover, redirects, HEAD and Range. This corrects the older PLAYBACK_SECRET-empty fail-open finding. Production DNS/TLS/origin deployment, Backend public-object origin behavior and real private-media staging acceptance remain separate release gates.

authority: signed delivery of Backend-authorized public Create activities
public dereferencing of Backend-canonical ActivityPub Notes
services.auth: Public ActivityPub ingress uses HTTP Signatures; Backend-to-Federation uses a distinct service bearer; Federation-to-Backend uses a different service bearer
services.notes: Backend publishes authorized activities to the private /internal/v1/activities ingress using a dedicated direction-specific service bearer and activity ID idempotency key. Federation authenticates the ingress, verifies Backend actor eligibility, durably enqueues the outbox item and acknowledges 202 only after acceptance. Federation-to-Backend uses a separate bearer. Public routing, inbound activity projections, delivery workers and external-peer interoperability remain gated; durable acceptance is not proof of delivery.

authority: ranking order and ranking scores only
services.notes: Backend submits at most 200 already-authorized candidates to POST /v1/feed/rank and requests at most 50 results. The pinned Backend client and Algorithm OpenAPI agree on the path and API-version/service-bearer headers. Backend rejects unknown/duplicate IDs and rechecks current authorization before hydration. Staging service-authentication, timeout/fallback and load acceptance remain required.
